big_case.notes: Although disqualifying the elected Attorney General of Guam's entire office in a public-corruption prosecution of Guam Regional Transit Authority officials carries meaningful institutional significance within the territory, the petition presented a poor vehicle with negligible national doctrinal reach: the Superior Court disqualified the office under Guam Rule of Professional Conduct 1.7(a)(2) after finding an unscreened concurrent conflict of interest and held the Attorney General's separation-of-powers arguments untimely under local rules, and the Supreme Court of Guam dismissed the appeal on an unpublished procedural order enforcing the unstayed disqualification order when no substitute counsel appeared. The Court denied certiorari at its first conference without requesting a response or noting any dissent.
